problem_text:
A regional wildlife tracking expedition must deploy sensor stations across eight distinct forest reserves:
Reserve Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (51,30)
Reserve Beta: Positioned at grid reference (127,101)
Reserve Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (65,53)
Reserve Delta: Positioned at grid reference (164,10)
Reserve Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (55,159)
Reserve Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (37,26)
Reserve Eta: Positioned at grid reference (50,117)
Reserve Theta: Positioned at grid reference (96,92)

The travel distances between reserves, measured in kilometers along established ranger paths, are as follows:
Alpha to Gamma: 26.9 km
Alpha to Delta: 114.8 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 129.1 km
Alpha to Zeta: 14.6 km
Alpha to Eta: 87.0 km
Alpha to Theta: 76.6 km
Beta to Gamma: 78.4 km
Beta to Delta: 98.2 km
Beta to Epsilon: 92.5 km
Beta to Zeta: 117.2 km
Beta to Eta: 78.6 km
Beta to Theta: 32.3 km
Gamma to Delta: 107.9 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 106.5 km
Gamma to Zeta: 38.9 km
Gamma to Eta: 65.7 km
Gamma to Theta: 49.8 km
Delta to Epsilon: 184.6 km
Delta to Zeta: 128.0 km
Delta to Eta: 156.3 km
Delta to Theta: 106.5 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 134.2 km
Epsilon to Eta: 42.3 km
Epsilon to Theta: 78.5 km
Zeta to Eta: 91.9 km
Zeta to Theta: 88.5 km
Eta to Theta: 52.4 km

Due to a seasonal river flooding, a direct path between Reserve Alpha and Reserve Beta is currently impassable.
Furthermore, owing to a logistical constraint regarding bridge maintenance, exactly one of the following two critical corridors must be incorporated into the circuit: the path between Reserve Beta and Reserve Gamma, or the path between Reserve Gamma and Reserve Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a single expedition team to visit each reserve precisely once for sensor deployment, ultimately concluding its journey back at the initial starting reserve.
